'''Gu Leguan''' ({{lang-zh|s=顾乐观|t=顧樂觀|p=Gù Lèguān}}; January 1935 – 2001) was a Chinese physicist and educator. He served as [[President of Chongqing University]] from December 1986 to August 1992, and [[Chinese Communist Party Committee Secretary|Communist Party Secretary]] of Chongqing University, from August 1989 to April 1997.<ref>{{cite web|author=|url=http://www.cqu.edu.cn/Channel/CquHistoryLeader/1/index.html|script-title=zh:重庆大学历任领导|publisher=Chongqing University|date=1 May 2015|access-date=1 May 2015|language=zh|archive-date=15 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200615045820/http://www.cqu.edu.cn/Channel/CquHistoryLeader/1/index.html|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://news.cqu.edu.cn/news/info/article_2477.html  |script-title=zh:光荣之路—重庆大学历任校长知多少 |publisher=Chongqing University  |date=2009 |access-date=1 May 2015 |language=zh |url-status=dead  |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150721040523/http://news.cqu.edu.cn/news/info/article_2477.html  |archivedate=2015-07-21  }}</ref>

==Biography==
{{Unreferenced section|date=April 2024}}
Gu was born and raised in [[Wu County]], [[Jiangsu]]. After high school, he studied, then taught, at [[Chongqing University]]. He earned his Ph.D. in Sciences and Engineering from [[Saint Petersburg State Polytechnic University]] in 1960s. After graduation, he returned to China and taught at Chongqing University. In December 1986 the [[Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party]] and the [[State Council of the People's Republic of China]] appointed him [[President of Chongqing University]], a position he held until August 1992. He also served as [[Chinese Communist Party Committee Secretary|Communist Party Secretary]] of Chongqing University, from August 1989 to April 1997. He died in 2001 in [[Chongqing]].
